_comment: Stance axes, one per product category. EDITORIAL by construction: choosing what the poles of an issue are is an argument, not a measurement, which is why this lives in a data file that can be challenged rather than inside code. Every axis is named from the POLICY DIRECTION, never from a political identity — 'more restriction' not 'anti-gun', 'more enforcement' not 'anti-immigrant'. A person is placed by what they said about policy; no axis is allowed to imply a tribe.
_scale: -1.0 = the negative pole, +1.0 = the positive pole, 0 = balanced or explicitly both-ways. null = the statement carries no position on this axis.

Healthcare and Public Health.neg: larger public role in health coverage
Healthcare and Public Health.pos: larger market role in health coverage

Education.neg: more public funding and public-school focus
Education.pos: more school choice and private options

Foreign Policy and National Security.pos: military strength and unilateral action first

Government Reform.neg: more transparency, ethics and voting access

Social Welfare Programs.pos: narrower safety net and more conditions

_known_gaps: The corpus predates the current technology debate almost entirely. Measured across all 531 people: 'artificial intelligence' appears 0 times, 'data center' 0, 'semiconductor' 0, 'crypto' 2, 'privacy' 3. Only 'surveillance' (55) and 'broadband' (17) have any volume. Any UI offering an AI or data-centre filter would be answering from nothing, and must not be built against this source.
